plan: 1 Samuel 26:1-25; 1 Samuel 27:1-7; 1 Chronicles 12:1-7; 1 Samuel 27:8-12; 1 Samuel 28:1-25; 1 Samuel 29:1-11; 1 Chronicles 12:19; Psalm 56:1-13

readings.title: Mercy at the Hill of Hakilah
readings.subtitle: Dawid Spares Sha'ul's Life a Second Time
readings.text: [1 Samuel 26:1] And the Ziphites came to Sha'ul at Gibeah, saying, “Is Dawid not hiding in the hill of Hakilah, opposite Yeshimon?” [2] And Sha'ul rose up and went down to the Wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Yisra'el with him, to seek <dn>את</dn> Dawid in the Wilderness of Ziph. [3] And Sha'ul encamped in the hill of Hakilah, which is opposite Yeshimon, by the way. But Dawid was staying in the wilderness, and he saw that Sha'ul came after him into the wilderness. [4] Dawid therefore sent out spies, and knew that Sha'ul had indeed come. [5] And Dawid rose up and came to the place where Sha'ul had encamped. And Dawid saw <dn>את</dn> the place where Sha'ul lay, and Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army. And Sha'ul was lying within the camp, with the people encamped all around him. [6] And Dawid answered and said to Ahimelek the Hittite and to Abishai son of Tseruyah, brother of Yo'ab, saying, “Who will go down with me to Sha'ul in the camp?” And Abishai said, “I shall go down with you.” [7] And Dawid and Abishai came to the people by night, and saw <dn>את</dn> Sha'ul lying asleep within the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. And Abner and the people lay all around him. [8] And Abishai said to Dawid, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has surrendered <dn>את</dn> your enemy into your hand this day. And now, please, let me strike him to the earth at once with the spear, and not a second time.” [9] But Dawid said to Abishai, “Do not destroy him, for who shall stretch out his hand against the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and be guiltless?” [10] And Dawid said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall certainly smite him, or his day come that he shall die, or he shall go out to battle and perish. [11] “Far be it from me, by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that I should stretch out <dn>את</dn> my hand against the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. But now, please, take <dn>את</dn> the spear that is by his head and <dn>את</dn> the jug of water, and let us go.” [12] So Dawid took <dn>את</dn> the spear and <dn>את</dn> the jug of water by Sha'ul's head, and they went away. And no man saw it or knew it or awoke. For they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had fallen on them. [13] Dawid then passed over to the other side, and stood on the top of a hill far away, a great distance being between them. [14] And Dawid called out to the people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, “Do you not answer, Abner?” And Abner answered and said, “Who are you, calling out to the sovereign?” [15] And Dawid said to Abner, “Are you not a man? And who is like you in Yisra'el? Why then have you not guarded <dn>את</dn> your master the sovereign? For one of the people came in to destroy your master the sovereign. [16] “This matter that you have done is not good. As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, you are sons of death, because you have not guarded <dn>את</dn> your master, the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And now see where the sovereign’s spear is, and <dn>את</dn> the jug of water that was by his head.” [17] And Sha'ul knew Dawid’s voice, and said, “Is that your voice, my son Dawid?” And Dawid said, “It is my voice, my master, O sovereign.” [18] And he said, “Why does my master pursue his servant? For what have I done, or what evil is in my hand? [19] “And now, please, let my master the sovereign hear <dn>את</dn> the words of his servant: If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has stirred you up against me, let <dn>Him</dn> accept an offering. But if it is the children of men, they are cursed before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for they have driven me out today that I should not share in the inheritance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, ‘Go, serve other mighty ones.’ [20] “And now, do not let my blood fall to the earth before the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For the sovereign of Yisra'el has come out to seek a flea, as when one hunts a partridge in the mountains.” [21] And Sha'ul said, “I have sinned. Return, my son Dawid. For I do you no more evil, because my life was precious in your eyes today. See, I have acted foolishly, and have erred exceedingly.” [22] And Dawid answered and said, “See the spear of the sovereign! Let one of the young men come over and get it. [23] “And let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> repay every man for his righteousness and his truth, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave you into my hand today, but I would not stretch out <dn>את</dn> my hand against the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [24] “And see, as your life was valued in my eyes today, so let my life be valued in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and let <dn>Him</dn> deliver me out of all distress.” [25] And Sha'ul said to Dawid, “Blessed are you, my son Dawid. You shall both do great deeds and certainly prevail.” And Dawid went on his way, and Sha'ul returned to his place.

readings.title: Flight to Gath and Tsiqlag
readings.subtitle: Dawid Seeks Refuge Among the Philistines
readings.text: [1 Samuel 27:1] And Dawid said in his heart, “Now I shall perish someday by the hand of Sha'ul. There is naught better for me than to certainly escape to the land of the Philistines. And Sha'ul shall despair of me, to seek me anymore in any part of Yisra'el, and I shall escape out of his hand.” [2] So Dawid rose up and passed over with <dn>את</dn> the six hundred men who were with him to Akhish son of Ma'ok, sovereign of Gath. [3] And Dawid dwelt with Akhish at Gath, he and his men, each man with his household, Dawid with <dn>את</dn> his two wives, <dn>את</dn> Ahino'am the Yizre'elitess, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇigayil the Karmelitess, Nabal’s widow. [4] And it was reported to Sha'ul that Dawid had fled to Gath, so he sought him no more. [5] And Dawid said to Akhish, “If I have now found favour in your eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I might dwell there. For why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?” [6] And Akhish gave him <dn>את</dn> Tsiqlag that day. Therefore Tsiqlag belongs to the sovereigns of Yehudah to this day. [7] And the days that Dawid dwelt in the country of the Philistines was a year and four months. [1 Chronicles 12:1] And these were the men who came to Dawid at Tsiqlag while he was still a fugitive from Sha'ul son of Qish. And they were among the mighty men, helpers in the battle, [2] armed with bows, using both the right hand and the left in hurling stones and shooting arrows with the bow. They were of the brothers of Sha'ul from Binyamin: [3] Ahiezer the chief, and Yo'ash the sons of Shema'ah the Gib'athite, and Yeziel, and Pelet the sons of Azmaweth, and Berakah, and Yehu the Anthothite, [4] and Yishmayah the Gib'onite, a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty, and Yirmeyah, and Yahaziel, and Yohanan, and Yozabad the Gederathite, [5] Eluzai, and Yerimoth, and Bealyah, and Shemaryahu, and Shephatyahu the Hariphite, [6] Elqanah, and Yishshiyah, and Azar'el, and Yo'ezer, and Yashob'am, the Qorhites, [7] and Yo'elah, and Zebadyah the sons of Yeroham of Gedor.

readings.title: A Mikhtam of Dawid
readings.subtitle: When the Philistines Captured Him in Gath
readings.text: [Psalm 56:1] Show favour to me, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, for man would swallow me up; Fighting all day he oppresses me. [2] My enemies would swallow me up all day, For many are fighting against me, O <dn>Most High</dn>. [3] In the day I am afraid, I put my trust in <dn>You</dn>. [4] In <dn>Elohim</dn>, whose Word I praise, In <dn>Elohim</dn> I have put my trust; I do not fear. What could flesh do to me? [5] All day long they twist my words; All their thoughts are against me for evil. [6] They stir up strife, They hide, they watch my steps, As they waited for my life. [7] Because of wickedness cast them out! In displeasure bring down the peoples, O <dn>Elohim</dn>! [8] <dn>You</dn> have counted my wanderings; <dn>You</dn> put my tears into <dn>Your</dn> bottle; Are they not in <dn>Your</dn> book? [9] Then my enemies shall turn back in the day I call; This I know, because <dn>Elohim</dn> is for me. [10] In <dn>Elohim</dn>, whose Word I praise, In <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, whose Word I praise, [11] In <dn>Elohim</dn> I have put my trust; I do not fear. What could man do to me? [12] <dn>Your</dn> vows are upon me, O <dn>Elohim</dn>; I pay thank offerings to <dn>You</dn>. [13] For <dn>You</dn> have delivered my life from death, My feet from falling, To walk before <dn>Elohim</dn> in the light of the living.

readings.title: Raids from Tsiqlag
readings.subtitle: Dawid's Deception of Akhish
readings.text: [1 Samuel 27:8] And Dawid and his men went up and raided the Geshurites and the Girzites and the Amaleqites. For those limits were of old, as you go to Shur, even to the land of Mitsrayim. [9] And Dawid would smite <dn>את</dn> the land, and leave neither man nor woman alive, and take away the sheep, and the cattle, and the donkeys, and the camels, and the garments, and return and come to Akhish. [10] And Akhish would say, “Where have you made a raid today?” And Dawid would say, “Against the South of Yehudah,” or “Against the South of the Yerahme'elites,” or “Against the South of the Qenites.” [11] And Dawid would save neither man nor woman alive, to bring news to Gath, saying, “Lest they should report concerning us, saying, ‘Thus Dawid has done.’ ” And so was his behavior all the time he dwelt in the country of the Philistines. [12] And Akhish trusted Dawid, saying, “He has made his people Yisra'el to utterly stink of him! Therefore he shall be my servant forever.”

readings.title: The Medium of Ěn Dor
readings.subtitle: Sha'ul Consults the Dead in Desperation
readings.text: [1 Samuel 28:1] And it came to be in those days that the Philistines gathered <dn>את</dn> their armies for war, to fight with Yisra'el. And Akhish said to Dawid, “Know for certain that you will go out with me to battle, you and your men.” [2] And Dawid said to Akhish, “Therefore you shall know what your servant can do.” And Akhish said to Dawid, “Therefore I make you one of my chief guardians forever.” [3] And Shemu’ĕl had died, and all Yisra'el had lamented for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Sha'ul had put <dn>את</dn> the mediums and <dn>את</dn> the spiritists out of the land. [4] And the Philistines gathered, and came and encamped at Shunem. And Sha'ul gathered all Yisra'el, and they encamped at Gilboa. [5] And Sha'ul saw <dn>את</dn> the army of the Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly. [6] And Sha'ul inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did not answer him, neither by dreams nor by Urim nor by prophets. [7] Sha'ul then said to his servants, “Seek for me a woman who is a medium, so that I go to her and inquire of her.” And his servants said to him, “See, there is a woman who is a medium at Ěn Dor.” [8] And Sha'ul disguised himself and put on other garments, and he went, and two men with him. And they came to the woman by night. And he said, “Please divine for me, and bring up for me <dn>את</dn> the one I shall name to you.” [9] But the woman said to him, “Look, you know what Sha'ul has done, how he has cut off <dn>את</dn> the mediums and <dn>את</dn> the spiritists from the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to cause me to die?” [10] And Sha'ul swore to her by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, no punishment comes upon you for this matter.” [11] The woman then said, “Whom do I bring up for you?” And he said, “Bring up <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl for me.” [12] And the woman saw <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl, and she cried out with a loud voice. And the woman spoke to Sha'ul, saying, “Why have you deceived me? For you are Sha'ul!” [13] And the sovereign said to her, “Do not be afraid. What did you see?” And the woman said to Sha'ul, “I saw a god coming up out of the earth.” [14] And he said to her, “What is his form?” And she said, “An old man is coming up, and he is covered with a mantle.” And Sha'ul knew that it was Shemu’ĕl, and he bowed with his face to the ground and did obeisance. [15] And Shemu’ĕl said to Sha'ul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” And Sha'ul answered, “I am deeply distressed, for the Philistines are fighting against me, and <dn>Elohim</dn> has departed from me and does not answer me anymore, neither by prophets nor by dreams. Therefore I have called you to make known to me what I should do.” [16] And Shemu’ĕl said, “And why do you ask me, seeing <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has departed from you and has become your enemy? [17] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has done for <dn>Himself</dn> as <dn>He</dn> spoke by me. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has torn <dn>את</dn> the reign out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to Dawid. [18] “Because you did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> nor execute <dn>His</dn> fierce wrath upon Amaleq, therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has done this to you today. [19] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> also gives <dn>את</dn> Yisra'el with you into the hand of the Philistines. And tomorrow you and your sons are with me. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> also gives <dn>את</dn> the army of Yisra'el into the hand of the Philistines.” [20] And immediately Sha'ul fell straight down on the ground, and was greatly afraid because of the words of Shemu’ĕl. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no food all day or all night. [21] And the woman came to Sha'ul and saw that he was greatly troubled, and said to him, “See, your female servant has obeyed your voice, and I have put my life in my hands and listened to <dn>את</dn> the words which you spoke to me. [22] “And now, please listen to the voice of your female servant too, and let me set a piece of bread before you. And eat, so that you have strength when you go on your way.” [23] But he refused and said, “I do not eat.” However, his servants, together with the woman, urged him. And he listened to their voice, and rose from the ground and sat on the bed. [24] And the woman had a fatted calf in the house, and she hurried and killed it. And she took flour and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread from it. [25] And she brought it before Sha'ul and his servants, and they ate. Then they rose and went away that night.

readings.title: Rejected by the Philistine Commanders
readings.subtitle: Dawid is Sent Back from the Battle
readings.text: [1 Samuel 29:1] And the Philistines gathered <dn>את</dn> all their armies at Aphek, while Yisra'el encamped by a fountain which is in Yizre'el. [2] And the princes of the Philistines were passing on by hundreds and by thousands, and Dawid and his men were passing on in the rear with Akhish. [3] Then the commanders of the Philistines said, “What are these Hebrews doing here?” And Akhish said to the commanders of the Philistines, “Is this not Dawid, the servant of Sha'ul sovereign of Yisra'el, who has been with me these days, or these years? And to this day I have found no fault in him since he defected to me.” [4] But the commanders of the Philistines were wroth with him, and the commanders of the Philistines said to him, “Make <dn>את</dn> the man return, and let him go back to his place which you have appointed for him, and do not let him go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he become our adversary. For with what could he reconcile himself to his master, if not with the heads of these men? [5] “Is this not Dawid, of whom they sang to each other in dances, saying, ‘Sha'ul smote his thousands, and Dawid his ten thousands’?” [6] Akhish then called Dawid and said to him, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, you have been upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the army is good in my eyes. For to this day I have not found evil in you since the day of your coming to me. But in the eyes of the princes you are not good. [7] “And now, return, and go in peace, so that you do not do evil in the eyes of the princes of the Philistines.” [8] And Dawid said to Akhish, “But what have I done? And what have you found in your servant as long as I have been with you to this day, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my master the sovereign?” [9] And Akhish answered and said to Dawid, “I know that you are as good in my eyes as a messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>. However, the commanders of the Philistines have said, ‘He does not go up with us to the battle.’ [10] “And now, rise early in the morning with your master’s servants who have come with you. And as soon as you are up early in the morning and have light, depart.” [11] So Dawid and his men rose up early to depart in the morning, to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Yizre'el. [1 Chronicles 12:19] And some from Menashsheh defected to Dawid when he went with the Philistines to battle against Sha'ul. But they did not help them, for the princes of the Philistines by counsel sent him away, saying, “He would defect to his master Sha'ul at the cost of our heads.”
